question: Does signed expected internal force flux close the residual high-activity fielded-force divergence better than gross inbound transport pressure?

motivation_locked_from_prior_support.residual: 2/24 multiplicity-significant practically-large pairs, both high-activity and both final_logF only
motivation_locked_from_prior_support.mechanistic_hypothesis: Local fielded force follows a continuity decomposition with local source/sink terms plus signed internal transport flux; gross inbound pressure omits expected departures.

transport12v2: log1p gross inbound expected insurgent effective-strength transport
nettransport12v2: signed expected insurgent effective-strength net transport flux

signed_flux_definition: Expected incoming effective strength minus expected outgoing effective strength over the next command opportunity. Internal relocation is conservative by construction: sum_i T_i = 0 up to roundoff.
selection_rule: Prefer the lowest-dimensional candidate that passes every preregistered gate. If multiple equal-dimensional candidates pass, prefer lower raw practically-large pair rate, then lower median match distance. Do not change thresholds after seeing outcomes.

interpretation.net_single_pass: Signed transport flux is a sufficient transport coordinate on tested support; gross inbound flow is not required.
interpretation.both_only_pass: Inbound and outbound information are independently relevant; transport requires at least two coarse coordinates or an improved flux representation.
interpretation.all_fail: Force-flow closure requires an additional source/sink or movement-state coordinate; do not claim Markov closure.
